summary: This unit teaches you to prepare guest rooms in a hotel, guest house or villa to the property's standard. You will learn to read the room report, stock and use your trolley, enter rooms correctly, service departure and stayover rooms, strip and make beds with mitred corners, clean and restock bathrooms, dust, vacuum and check the room, give turn-down service, prepare a villa for a family, protect guests' security and belongings, and report faults and lost property.

blocks.p: A guest's first impression of a room comes in the first minute: the smell, the bed, the bathroom, the cool air. A room attendant is the person who makes that impression, usually working alone and unseen. A well-prepared room is clean, fresh, safe, complete and in working order. A poorly prepared one leads to complaints, bad reviews and lost guests.

This unit is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees. You will learn to service a room that a guest has left (a **departure**), a room where a guest is still staying (a **stayover**), give an evening **turn-down** and prepare a whole **villa** for arriving guests.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and group practical tasks in the Centre's mock villa: servicing a departure room, then giving a stayover service and an evening turn-down to an occupied room. The assessor watches your entry, bed making, safety, order of work and records.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.note: In practical work, use made-up guest details only. Never pick up needles or broken glass by hand; tell the assessor.
blocks.label: Safety

sections.title: Room status, the room report and your trolley

blocks.p: The housekeeping and front desk both need to know the state of each room. The code names vary between properties. These are the common ones; check your own property's list.

head: Code or word
Meaning
What you do
rows: VD (vacant dirty)
No guest, but the room needs cleaning.
Clean it fully.
VC (vacant clean)
Cleaned and waiting for inspection or the next guest.
Check it is still ready; an inspector may check it.
OC (occupied clean)
A guest is staying; the room has been serviced.
Leave alone until the next service.
OD (occupied dirty)
A guest is staying and the room needs service.
Do a stayover service.
Departure (check-out)
The guest has left today; full clean needed.
Strip, clean and reset.
Stayover
The guest is staying another night.
Lighter service; work round their things.
DND
Do Not Disturb: the guest does not want to be disturbed.
Do not knock. Follow the property's rule; record it.
OOO (out of order)
The room cannot be sold until a repair is done.
Do not clean unless told; do not enter without the supervisor.
OOS (out of service)
Taken out of use for a short time, for example for deep cleaning.
Follow the supervisor's instructions.
VIP
A very important person, such as a repeat guest or a special guest.
Prepare first and to the highest standard.
Early arrival
A guest is due before normal check-in time.
Prepare this room soon.

blocks.p: At the start of the shift, you collect your **room report** and key or key card from your supervisor and sign for them. The report lists your rooms and their status, and notes such as VIP guests, early arrivals, extra beds, baby cots and special requests.

ul: Plan the order of your rooms. **Do first** the rooms needed soonest: early arrivals, VIPs, and departure rooms the front desk is waiting for.
Then do stayover rooms when guests are out, and finish with the others.
Do not disturb a room with a DND sign; note it on your report and tell your supervisor.
Fill in the report as you go, and hand it in at the end of the shift.

blocks.p: Your trolley carries everything for your rooms, so you do not have to keep going back to the linen room. Load it at the start of the shift using your report: how many rooms, what types.

head: Place
What goes there
Why
rows: Bottom shelf
Heavy items: stacks of sheets and duvet covers
Keeps the trolley stable so it does not tip.
Middle shelf
Towels, pillowcases, bath mats
Easy to reach.
Top shelf
Guest amenities (soap, shampoo, lotion), toilet tissue, tea and coffee, stationery, glasses
Small items are easy to see and lift.
Side bags
Dirty linen bag and rubbish bag (empty and fixed in place)
Keeps dirty items away from clean ones.
Caddy or tray
Cloths, brushes, gloves and chemicals, in labelled containers
Chemicals must be kept apart from clean linen.

ul: Check the trolley is clean and its wheels run well.
Count and record the linen and supplies you take for your floor, so stock can be controlled and reordered in time.
Keep chemicals away from clean linen; keep them locked on the trolley when not in use.

blocks.note: Park the trolley **across the open doorway** of the room you are cleaning. It shows that the room is being serviced, it blocks entry by strangers, and it lets you see the corridor. Never leave the trolley unattended with the master key on it.
blocks.label: Safety

sections.title: Entering a room and keeping it secure

flow: Check the door for a DND sign
Park the trolley across the doorway
Knock firmly and say 'Housekeeping'
Wait, then knock and announce again
Open the door slowly, announce again, then enter
If the guest is in, apologise and ask when it would suit them for you to clean
Leave the door open while you work

head: Situation
What to do
rows: DND sign on the door
Do not knock; come back later and follow the property's rules (usually the supervisor decides after a set time).
Guest is in the room when you enter
Apologise and ask when it would suit them for you to clean; come back later.
Guest asleep
Leave quietly; come back later; tell your supervisor.
A person in the corridor says it is their room and asks you to open it
Do not open it. Politely send them to the front desk, where they show ID and get a key.
A visitor asks for a guest's room number
Do not give it. Refer them to the front desk.
You need to fetch towels from the linen store
Close and lock the room door, and check it is locked.

ul: Keep your master key or key card on you at all times, on a cord or clip. Never lend it or leave it in a door or on the trolley.
Do not say a guest's name or room number aloud where others might hear.
Do not touch, open or read guests' belongings. Do not use their phone, toilet or things.
Report anything unusual, such as a smell of gas, an unknown person in a room or a door left open.

blocks.note: In a departure room, switch on the lights to check the bulbs, open the curtains and air the room before you start. This lets you see what needs doing and helps remove smells.
blocks.label: Tip

blocks.p: A departure room has been left by the guest, so everything is stripped, cleaned, checked and reset for the next guest. Work in the same order every time, so nothing is missed: **high to low, clean to dirty, dry to wet**, with the vacuum last.

flow: Enter correctly; switch on lights, open curtains, air the room
Check for items left by the guest, and for damage or missing items; report them
Remove rubbish, used glasses, cups and trays
Strip the bed slowly, looking for needles or guest items; linen straight into the bag
Check the mattress and protector for stains, damage and bed bugs
Make the bed with fresh linen
Clean the bathroom: cleanest parts to the toilet, floor last
Restock towels, toilet tissue and amenities
Dust from high to low; clean mirrors and glass; check the equipment
Vacuum, working back to the door
Check the room as a guest would; fill in forms; lock the room; update the status

ul: Anything the guest left, even something small like a phone charger, is **handed in as lost property** and logged. Never keep it.
Look for damage: stains, burns, broken items, missing items, marks on walls. Report on the maintenance form before you tidy, so the damage is recorded.
Check the minibar if the property has one, and report what has been used, so the front desk can charge it.
Check the room safe is empty and working.
Strip it slowly and look carefully: needles, glass or guest items can be caught in the linen.
Never pick up needles or broken glass by hand. Use a sharps box or tongs and report it. A used syringe in a bin: leave it, keep others away and report it at once.
Put dirty linen straight into the linen bag on the trolley, not on the floor. Do not hug dirty linen to your uniform.
Take pillowcases off, and look at each pillow for stains.

Check the mattress protector, the mattress seams and the headboard for bed bugs (small brown insects, blood spots, dark specks). If you see any, stop, tell your supervisor and do not move linen from that room.

blocks.note: Bend your knees and keep your back straight when you lift mattresses or make beds. Pull the bed out a little so you can walk round it instead of reaching over. Ask for help to turn a heavy mattress.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: Dust from high to low: curtain rails, tops of picture frames, lamp shades, headboard, furniture, skirting boards. The tops of picture frames, lamp shades and headboards are often missed.
Clean mirrors and glass without smears.
Check that lights, TV, remote control, air conditioning, hair dryer, phone and safe all work. Report any fault.
Check the minibar, tea and coffee set and glasses are clean and complete.
Vacuum last, working from the far side back to the door, because dust and crumbs fall to the floor during the other jobs.

head: Layer
Notes
rows: Mattress protector
A washable, often waterproof cover over the mattress. Check it is clean, smooth and not damaged.
Bottom sheet
Fitted or flat. Centre fold down the middle of the bed, right side up, equal overhang each side.
Top sheet
Right side down, hem at the head of the bed.
Blanket, if used
Placed below the top fold, tucked in at the foot.
Duvet (a thick soft quilt in a cover)
Shake it into the cover; corners filled; the cover lies smooth.
Pillows and pillowcases
Fresh cases, pillows filled to the corners; open end away from the door.
Bed runner
A long, narrow decorative cloth laid across the foot of the bed.

blocks.h: Making the bed with mitred corners

flow: Pull the bed out a little so you can walk round; check the mattress protector
Put on the bottom sheet, centre fold down the middle; tuck in firmly at the head, then at the foot
To make a mitred (hospital) corner, lift the hanging sheet about 30 cm from the corner up onto the mattress, making a slanted fold
Tuck in the part that hangs below the mattress
Drop the folded part over the side and tuck it in, making a neat 45-degree corner
Repeat on each corner and then the sides; pull the sheet tight
Put on the top sheet, hem at the head, right side down; tuck in at the foot and make mitred corners
Fold the top sheet back at the head; add the blanket or duvet
Put on fresh pillowcases and place the pillows with the open end away from the door
Smooth the bed and add any decoration; check that it looks neat from the door

blocks.p: A **mitred (hospital) corner** is a neat, folded corner that holds the sheet tight and flat. It stops the sheets coming loose and gives the bed a smart look. Linen is changed every departure; in stayovers it follows the property's standard or the guest's green card.

blocks.note: Make the bed from the sides, not by leaning across it. Walk round the bed, so you do not strain your back. Work with the bed pulled slightly from the wall.
blocks.label: Safety

head: Type
Set-up
rows: Single
One single bed, for one guest.
Twin
Two single beds, for two guests.
Double or queen or king
One large bed, for one or two guests.
Suite
A bedroom with a separate sitting area.
Extra bed or cot
Added on request; check it is safe.
Accessible room
Wide doors, grab rails and a roll-in shower, for guests who use wheelchairs.

blocks.p: Many hotels and villas have a **green card** that the guest can leave on the bed to say they are happy to keep the same sheets and towels, to save water, detergent and energy. Follow the card: if it is on the bed, do not change the sheets, but still tidy the bed and replace towels the guest has left on the floor.
The bathroom needs the most care, because it is where germs and bad smells collect and guests judge cleanliness hardest.

ul: Put on gloves, and goggles if you use a strong product. Collect your caddy with colour-coded cloths and the right chemicals.
Read each label and dilute as it says. Never mix products, especially bleach with acid or ammonia cleaners; they give off a poisonous gas.
Ventilate: switch on the extractor fan or open the window.
Put a wet floor sign at the door if the floor will be wet.

flow: Remove used towels, mats and rubbish
Flush the toilet and apply toilet cleaner under the rim so it has time to work
Clean the mirror and glass shelves
Clean the basin, taps and counter
Clean the shower or bath, glass, taps and drain; remove hair
Clean the toilet last of the fittings: outside, seat, then bowl with the brush
Wipe the walls and tiles where needed
Mop the floor last, from the far corner to the door
Restock towels, mats, tissue and amenities; check bins and the extractor fan

head: Rule
Why
rows: Clean from the cleanest parts to the toilet; floor last
So you do not spread germs from the toilet to other surfaces.
Use a cloth kept **only for toilets**, as the colour code says
To stop germs from the toilet spreading to the basin and glasses.
Put toilet cleaner in the bowl at the start
So it has time to work while you clean other parts.
Change glasses, or wash them as the rules say
Guests drink from them.
Wipe taps, shower glass and tiles dry
Water left to dry leaves marks.

blocks.note: In many Jamaican homes and hotels the water is hard (it contains dissolved lime). When it dries, it leaves white, chalky marks on taps and shower glass. Lime scale is removed with a descaler, which is an acid cleaner. Use it only on surfaces that allow it, and never mix it with bleach.
blocks.label: Jamaica

ul: Put out the set number of towels, bath mats, soap, shampoo, lotion and toilet tissue, as the property's standard says. Too few annoy guests; too many waste stock.
Place amenities neatly with labels facing the front.
Fold the end of a new toilet roll into a neat point to show it is fresh, if the property does this.
Check the bin has a clean liner.

head: Problem found
What to do
rows: Dripping tap, blocked drain, loose toilet seat
Report to maintenance on a work order.
Mould on grout or ceiling
Clean with the right product and PPE; report the cause.
Used syringe or sharp item in a bin
Do not touch. Keep others away and report at once.
Guest's toiletries left
Handle as lost property if the guest has checked out.

blocks.p: A **stayover** service is cleaning a room while the guest is still staying. It is lighter than a departure service, and you must respect the guest's belongings and privacy.

head: Departure room
Stayover room
rows: The guest has gone; everything is stripped and reset.
The guest is staying; you work round their things.
Linen is fully changed.
Linen is changed as the standard or green card says.
All items checked and left items handed in.
Leave papers, jewellery and belongings where they are; dust round them.
Everything restocked.
Replace used amenities and towels left out to be changed.
Amenities replaced completely.
Throw away only what is in the waste bins.

ul: Knock and announce yourself; if the guest is in, ask if it is a good time.
Make the bed. Clothes left on the bed: fold them neatly or leave them, as the rules say.
Replace towels the guest has left on the floor; leave towels they have hung up if the green card says so.
Empty the bins, clean the bathroom, restock, dust round belongings, vacuum.
Never move, open or read guests' belongings; never throw anything away except what is in the bins.
Report anything you see that worries you, such as a sharps box in the room or signs of illness.

blocks.p: **Turn-down** is an evening service, often given while the guests are at dinner, to get the room ready for sleep.

flow: Check the room report for rooms that want turn-down
Knock, announce and, if the guest is in, ask whether they want it now or later
Empty the bins; remove used glasses and trays
Tidy the room without moving belongings
Fold back the bed cover or duvet at an angle on the side the guest sleeps; plump the pillows
Place the amenities, such as a chocolate or a card, on the pillow or bedside table
Close the curtains; set the lights and the air conditioning as the property's standard says
Freshen the bathroom: replace used towels, tidy the counter, wipe the basin
Check that all is in place, lock the door and record it on the room report

blocks.note: Turn-down is a chance to make the guest feel special, but it is also a chance to make mistakes. Never go through a guest's bags, never use their phone and never leave a mess. If a guest says no, thank them and leave.
blocks.label: Tip

blocks.p: A villa is a whole home for the guests: bedrooms, kitchen, living room, pool or garden. Preparing it means all of the departure work in every room, plus extra checks and welcome touches.

ul: **Read the booking notes:** the number of guests, the beds needed, and special requests such as a baby cot, extra towels, or food allergies.
**Beds and bathrooms:** every bedroom made up to standard with the right number of pillows and towels, including pool and beach towels.

**Check everything works:** lights, ceiling fans, air conditioning, TV, Wi-Fi card, taps, toilets, hot water, door locks, windows and room safe. Report any fault at once so it is fixed before arrival.
**Kitchen:** clean and stocked as the property's standard says: pots, plates, glasses, cutlery, cloths, washing-up liquid, bin liners, tea, coffee and drinking water.
**Outside:** the veranda, pool area and garden swept and tidy; furniture wiped; cushions in place.
**Air conditioning:** switch it on for a while before the guests arrive so that the rooms are cool and fresh.
**Welcome basket:** if the manager asks for fresh fruit, put it out as close to arrival as you can, so it is fresh.
**Final walk-round:** look at every room as a guest would, switch lights and fans off or on as the standard says, lock up and update the status.

head: Check
Why
rows: Air conditioning on before arrival
The villa is cool when guests walk in, and you find faults before they do.
All taps and toilets run
Leaks, blocks and no hot water are common complaints.
Smoke alarm or safety items present
Guests' safety, as the property's standard says.
Mosquito screens, nets and windows in good order
Mosquitoes can spread dengue and spoil sleep.
Welcome notes and information
Guests need Wi-Fi details, emergency numbers and the manager's number.

blocks.note: In Jamaica a villa near the sea may have been shut for days. Open the windows to air the rooms, check for damp, mould, pests and insects, and tell the manager of anything you find before the guests arrive.
blocks.label: Jamaica

head: Risk
How to work safely
rows: Back injury from beds, mattresses and the trolley
Bend your knees, walk round the bed, ask for help, push the trolley, do not pull it.
Chemicals
Read labels and SDS; measure dilutions; wear gloves and eye protection; ventilate; never mix products.
Needles, broken glass
Never pick up by hand; use a sharps box or tongs; report at once.
Slips on wet floors
Wipe up water at once; use signs.
Electric shock
Keep the vacuum cable out of walkways; switch off and unplug after use; do not touch plugs with wet hands.
Bed bugs and pests
Look at the mattress seams and headboard; report at once; do not carry linen from that room.
Infection from dirty linen
Put it straight in the bag; do not hold it against your uniform; wash your hands.

ul: Report faults quickly, so they are fixed **before a guest is upset or hurt**: a dripping tap, a broken light, a loose handle.
Use the property's system: a maintenance form or work order, with room, fault and time.
Count and record linen and supplies, so stock can be controlled and reordered in time.
Log left items as lost property, with the room, item, date and your name.
**Update the room status** as soon as a room is ready, so the front desk knows it can give the room to a guest. A clean room that shows as dirty wastes the property's chance to sell it.

blocks.p: Before you leave the room, **check it as a guest would**: stand at the door, look at the bed, bathroom, floor and furniture; check every light and switch; smell the air; make sure nothing is left behind, such as cloths or products. Then close and lock the door and update the status.

blocks.note: Never rush a room to make up time. A rushed room means a missed fault or a missed hair in the bath, and that means a complaint.
blocks.label: Remember

ul: read the room report and tell VD, VC, OC, DND, OOO, VIP and early arrival apart
plan the order of my rooms, doing early arrivals and VIPs first
load a trolley with heavy items low and chemicals apart from clean linen
park the trolley across the doorway and enter correctly: knock, announce, wait, repeat
respect Do Not Disturb and deal with a guest who is in the room
refuse politely to let a stranger into a room and keep my key on me
service a departure room in the correct order
strip a bed carefully and spot sharps and bed bugs
make a bed with a mattress protector, mitred corners, top sheet or duvet and pillows
clean a bathroom from the cleanest parts to the toilet, with the floor last
use colour-coded cloths and never mix chemicals
restock the amenities to the property's standard
dust from high to low and vacuum last
give a stayover service and an evening turn-down
prepare a villa for a family, including checks and the welcome basket
report faults, hand in left items, count stock and update the room status

terms: The sheet listing your rooms, their status and notes for the shift.
A room whose guest has checked out and needs a full clean.
A room where the guest is staying another night.
A room with no guest that needs cleaning.
A room that cannot be sold until a repair is done.
The wheeled cart that carries linen and supplies.
The room on each floor where clean linen and supplies are kept.
A washable, often waterproof cover over the mattress.
A neat folded corner that holds a sheet tight and flat.
A thick soft quilt in a cover, used instead of blankets.
A long narrow decorative cloth across the foot of a bed.
A card a guest can leave on the bed to keep the same sheets.
An evening service to get the room ready for sleep.
Guest supplies such as soap, shampoo and lotion.
A small fridge in a room holding drinks and snacks for sale.
A small locked box in a room for guests' valuables.
A fitting on the inside of a door that lets a guest open it a little.
A container for used needles, so no one is hurt.

A room set up for guests who use wheelchairs.

c1.title: Planning the day at a hotel in Ocho Rios
c1.text: Room attendant Shanice starts at 8 a.m. at an Ocho Rios hotel. Her room report lists 12 rooms: four departures, five stayovers, one VIP early arrival due at 10 a.m., one room marked OOO, and one stayover room with a Do Not Disturb sign. She has not yet loaded her trolley.

c2.title: A departure room in Mandeville
c2.text: Trainee Rushane is servicing a departure room at a Mandeville guest house. While stripping the bed, he sees a small dark brown insect in the mattress seam and a few dark specks on the headboard. In the bathroom bin he sees a used needle. On the desk is a phone charger and a book that the guest left behind.

c3.title: A bathroom at a villa in Negril
c3.text: Trainee Kerry-Ann is cleaning the bathroom at a Negril villa. She has bleach-based cleaner and a descaler (acid) for the white chalky marks on the shower glass and taps. She has a red cloth for toilets and a blue cloth for other surfaces. The window is small.

c4.title: A stayover room with a green card
c4.text: Trainee Andre is servicing an occupied room in Montego Bay. A green card is on the bed. The guest, Mr. Lewis, has left papers, a watch and some cash on the desk, and a towel on the bathroom floor. The guest is not in the room.

c5.title: Preparing a villa for a family in Port Antonio
c5.text: A family of five arrives at 3 p.m. at a villa in Port Antonio. The booking notes ask for a baby cot, extra towels, and no feather pillows. The manager has asked for a fresh fruit welcome basket in the kitchen. The villa has been empty for a week. Trainee Tameka is preparing it.

c6.title: Keys and security in a Kingston hotel
c6.text: Room attendant Odane is cleaning room 214 at a Kingston hotel. Her trolley is parked across the doorway. She needs to fetch towels from the linen store at the end of the corridor. Later, after finishing the floor, she reaches for her master key card on its cord and finds that the cord has snapped and the card is gone. She last remembers having it in room 209.

questions.q: Which room should Shanice prepare first?
o: The VIP early arrival room, which is due at 10 a.m. today
The stayover room that has the Do Not Disturb sign on its door
The room marked OOO, so that it can be sold to a guest later
The first departure room on the list, because it is first listed
questions.why: Rooms needed soonest, such as early arrivals and VIP guests, come first unless the supervisor says otherwise. DND rooms are not disturbed and OOO rooms cannot be sold.

questions.q: What should Shanice do about the room marked OOO?
o: Clean it first, as it is probably the dirtiest of all the rooms
Not clean or enter it unless the supervisor tells her to
Put a guest in it if the hotel is full, as it is only a small repair
Remove the OOO mark so that the room shows as vacant clean
questions.why: An out-of-order room cannot be sold until a repair is done. Only the supervisor decides whether it is cleaned or entered, and the status is changed only when it is ready.

questions.q: How should Shanice load her trolley?
o: Chemicals on the top shelf so that they are easy to reach quickly
Towels on the bottom shelf, because they are the heaviest of all
Everything in one pile on the middle shelf, to save time
Heavy items low, and chemicals kept apart from clean linen
questions.why: Heavy stacks go on the bottom shelf so the trolley does not tip. Chemicals must be kept apart from clean linen and locked when not in use.

questions.q: At the end of her shift, what should Shanice do with her room report?
o: Take it home with her so that she can plan tomorrow's rooms
Throw it away, because all of the rooms on it are finished
Fill it in as she goes and hand it to her supervisor
Leave it on the trolley overnight for the night shift to find
questions.why: The report is filled in as rooms are done and handed in at the end of the shift. It tells the supervisor and the front desk which rooms are ready, and what is still outstanding.

questions.q: What should Rushane do about the insect and the dark specks?
o: Stop, tell the supervisor, and not move linen out of the room
Wash the sheets as normal and continue to make the bed up as usual
Spray the mattress with room freshener and carry on with the room
Brush the insect away and throw the pillows into the rubbish bin
questions.why: Insects in mattress seams with dark specks may be bed bugs. Report at once; moving linen could spread them to other rooms.

questions.q: To check under the mattress for pests, Rushane must turn it over. It is heavy and the bed is against the wall. What is the safest way?
o: Pull the bed out, bend his knees and ask a colleague to help
Lift it by himself, as quickly as he can, to save time on the room
Push it from one side while leaning right across the bed to do it
Lift one corner and slide his arm under it to feel for any pests
questions.why: Mattresses are heavy and awkward, and back injury is a major risk. Pull the bed out so you can walk round it, bend your knees, keep your back straight and get help.

questions.q: What is the right way to deal with the phone charger and the book left behind?
o: Keep them safely until the guest calls to collect them
Hand them in as lost property and log them
Leave them on the desk for the next guest to find
Take them home in case the guest never returns
questions.why: Items left by a guest who has checked out are handed in and logged, so they can be returned. They are never kept or left in the room.

questions.q: Why should Rushane strip the bed slowly?
o: So that he is paid for more time spent working on the room
To avoid creasing the sheets before they are sent to be washed
Because the mattress is easily damaged by quick movements
Sharp items or a guest's things may be caught in it
questions.why: Needles, glass or small guest items can hide in bed linen. Stripping slowly and carefully protects you and finds left items.

questions.q: What is the main danger in Kerry-Ann's cleaning products?
o: Bleach and an acid descaler give off a poisonous gas if mixed
Bleach is too weak to clean a shower properly, even on its own
A descaler is likely to stain the white shower glass and the taps
Both of the products will damage the toilet cloth that she uses
questions.why: Never mix bleach with an acid cleaner or with ammonia; they release a poisonous gas. Use one product at a time, rinse well, and keep the room ventilated.

questions.q: What is the best way for Kerry-Ann to remove the chalky marks from the taps?
o: Rub them hard with a dry cloth until they shine again
Scour them with bleach powder and a stiff scrubbing brush
Spray them with a glass cleaner and then leave it on overnight
Use a descaler as the label says, then rinse and dry the taps
questions.why: Lime scale is dissolved by an acid descaler used as the label says, then rinsed and dried. Never mix it with bleach, and keep the room ventilated.

questions.q: Which cloth should Kerry-Ann use for the toilet, and why?
o: The blue cloth, as it will be washed afterwards in any case
Either cloth will do, as long as she rinses it out well afterwards
The red cloth, kept only for the toilet, to stop germs spreading
A guest's face cloth from the room, as it is soft and quite clean
questions.why: A cloth kept only for toilets, as the colour code says, stops germs from the toilet reaching the basin, taps and glasses.

questions.q: In what order should Kerry-Ann clean the bathroom?
o: Floor first, then the toilet, then the basin, taps and mirror
The toilet first, since it is the dirtiest, then the basin and floor
Cleanest parts first, ending with the toilet and then the floor
Whichever parts she can see are dirtiest first, in any order at all
questions.why: Cleaning from the cleanest parts to the toilet, with the floor last, avoids spreading germs from the dirtiest area to the cleaner ones.

questions.q: What should Andre do about the papers, watch and cash on the desk?
o: Put them in the room safe to keep them secure
Leave them where they are and dust round them
Move them to the bedside table while he cleans the desk
Count the cash and leave a note with the amount
questions.why: In an occupied room, guests' belongings are left where they are and cleaned round. Do not move, open or count them, as that could lead to a suspicion of theft.

questions.q: A green card is on the bed. What does it mean?
o: The guest wants the room to be cleaned twice on that day
The guest has asked for new towels and extra amenities to be left
The guest is happy to keep the same sheets, to save water
The guest has gone out and the room can be locked up for the day
questions.why: A green card means the guest chooses to keep the same sheets. Tidy the bed but do not change the linen, and still replace towels left on the floor.

questions.q: What should Andre do about the towel on the bathroom floor?
o: Leave it where it is, as the guest may want to use it again later
Take it away and not replace it, to save on the laundry work
Replace it with a fresh towel, as the guest left it to be changed
Hang it up neatly and leave the same towel in the bathroom for later
questions.why: A towel on the floor is the usual sign that the guest wants it changed. Replace it, and leave any towels that are hung up as the green card says.

questions.q: When should Tameka put out the welcome fruit basket?
o: Two days earlier, so that the kitchen is ready before they come
As close to arrival as she can, so that the fruit is fresh
On the morning of the day before the family are due to arrive
After the family arrive and have had a chance to settle in
questions.why: Fresh fruit looks and tastes best when put out close to arrival. Left for days in a warm Jamaican villa it spoils and attracts insects.

questions.q: Why should Tameka switch the air conditioning on before the family arrives?
o: To save on electricity during the hot part of the afternoon
So the rooms are cool, and any fault is found before arrival
Because guests are asked to pay for the time spent cooling the rooms
So that the air conditioning does not need to be serviced as often
questions.why: The villa is cool when the guests walk in, and a fault is reported and fixed before it spoils their arrival.

questions.q: The booking says 'no feather pillows'. What should Tameka do?
o: Use feather pillows, as the covers will keep the feathers in
Take the pillows from another villa without checking them
Put out any pillows, and tell the family to ask if they want others
Put out hypoallergenic pillows with fresh covers, and note it
questions.why: Special requests in the booking must be met before arrival. Hypoallergenic pillows with fresh covers are put out and the room is noted for future stays.

questions.q: Odane cannot find her master key card. What should she do first?
o: Look for it quietly for an hour, so that nobody finds out she lost it
Report it to her supervisor at once, so rooms can be secured
Ask the guests in room 209 to look for it while she carries on cleaning
Wait until the end of her shift and tell the supervisor then
questions.why: A lost master key is a serious security risk to every room on the floor. Report it at once so the supervisor can secure the rooms and have the card cancelled. A hidden loss is far worse than an honest report.

questions.q: Odane needs to fetch towels from the linen store down the corridor. What should she do with the room?
o: Leave the door open, as her trolley is in front of it
Close and lock the door, and check that it is locked
Pull the door to and ask a passing guest to keep an eye on it
Take the master key off the trolley and leave it on the bed
questions.why: A room left open, even for a moment, is a risk to the guest's belongings. Close and lock it and check, and keep your key on you.
